tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on the user's situation/intent (failing Bedrock calls, invisible model behavior, KB returning nothing or stale answers) rather than internal mechanics, and explicitly lists many trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly ('Use it even if they do not mention invocation logging, IAM, service control policies...'). It is a dense but bounded paragraph, appropriate given the skill's broad scope across two check families.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a Bedrock call fails with an access, validation or throttling error, when nobody can see what the model is doing... Use it even if they do not mention invocation logging, IAM, service control policies, marketplace subscriptions, chunking, embedding models, vector stores or hybrid search by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but focused on domain-specific, non-obvious facts (check-ids, account-ID masking rules, area routing, guardrails specific to this workflow). It does not explain generic concepts like what Bedrock or a knowledge base is in general terms; everything is tailored to this review process.
tests.evidence: "You never invent a threshold: where AWS publishes no number the catalog marks it workload-specific and you report it as INFO."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (check catalogs, metrics, API quirks, procedures) is kept in references/ files and only summarized or routed to in the body. The 'Pick the area first' table and 'When to use/not use' sections are concise routing logic, not detailed reference dumps.
tests.evidence: "references/model-access-review.md: the model access and configuration review (router, procedure, checks before presenting, LLM-INV family, wrong answers, error handling, AWS docs)."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked with a markdown link in the body, in the routing table and/or the References section.
tests.evidence: "references/model-access-review.md" | "references/knowledge-base-review.md" ... and the References section links checks-model-invocation.md, checks-rag-knowledgebase.md, diagnosis-playbook.md, rag-review-playbook.md, collection-reference.md, metrics-and-logs.md, api-quirks.md, related-skills.md

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Links specify precise conditions for when to load each reference, e.g. tied to specific error types or review areas, and the References section explains what's inside each.
tests.evidence: "Name the area, then read its review file before the first API call. Each file holds the router, the step-by-step procedure..."

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/, no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/non-negotiable operations (read-only guardrails, account ID masking, chunk content suppression) are stated as strict rules, while flexible areas (which review area to run, how to present findings) are described with purpose and routing logic rather than rigid step sequences.
tests.evidence: "Read-only. Never call a mutating API... never call StartIngestionJob" vs "When a question spans both areas, run both reviews and present one report with one Scope line"

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tools as equal options; it routes deterministically to the correct reference file per question type, which functions as a clear default path rather than a menu.
tests.evidence: The routing table maps specific question types to exactly one "Read first" reference file and report template.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (pick area, read review file, follow procedure, cite check-ids, produce report) that applies to any Bedrock/KB review request, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: "Pick the area first... Name the area, then read its review file before the first API call."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The body includes an explicit Guardrails section with concrete, non-obvious corrections (e.g., never call StartIngestionJob, never echo account ID, mask ARNs, Retrieve probe limits) that function as gotchas for this domain.
tests.evidence: "Never echo a raw 12-digit account ID... Mask the account segment of any ARN quoted as evidence."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly provides two report templates in assets/ for its structured review outputs, satisfying the need for templates.
tests.evidence: "assets/bedrock-configuration-report-template.md" and "assets/rag-health-report-template.md": report formats for each area.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline templates appear in the body; templates are stored in assets/ and only referenced, consistent with best practice.
tests.evidence: Only a severity table and routing table appear inline; no full report template skeleton is embedded in the body.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Both asset files are referenced in the body: in the routing table and in the References section.
tests.evidence: "assets/bedrock-configuration-report-template.md" and "assets/rag-health-report-template.md" appear in the routing table's 'Report template' column and in the References list.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Asset links are tied to specific review areas, telling the agent to use the configuration report template for model-access questions and the RAG health template for knowledge-base questions.
tests.evidence: "| Bedrock setup and best practice...| Model access and configuration | `references/model-access-review.md` | `assets/bedrock-configuration-report-template.md` |"

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: Asset references use relative paths from the skill root with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The body does not present an inline ordered, dependent step-by-step procedure in SKILL.md itself; the actual stepwise procedures live in the referenced review files (model-access-review.md, knowledge-base-review.md), while SKILL.md only does area routing, which is not itself a dependent multi-step workflow requiring a checklist.
tests.evidence: "Name the area, then read its review file before the first API call. Each file holds the router, the step-by-step procedure, the pre-presentation checks..."

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit guardrail requiring pre-presentation checks and evidence grounding, directing the agent to validate findings (check-ids, evidence, severity) before presenting, and delegates detailed pre-presentation checks to the area-specific reference files.
tests.evidence: "Evidence or silence. Every finding cites the concrete value that triggered it... A check-id on every finding... Each file holds... the pre-presentation checks..."
